children.name:
PROS Guidebook Adoption
      This will be the only reading of this item and final action may be taken. There will be one round of
      public comment.
children.desc:
Staff are seeking City Council’s adoption of the PROS Guidebook which contains both the Long Range Plan (LRP) and Trail System Plan (TSP).


Adoption would be the culmination of 28 months of planning, development and community engagement. The effort began with collecting feedback on the plan’s Request for Proposal (RFP) from Council and the PROS Advisory Boards. Consultant procurement then involved interviews with shortlisted firms and a Council presentation to refine the preferred consultant’s scope prior to contract authorization. Throughout the planning process, staff and consultants gathered valuable input on the broader community’s needs, desires, and priorities via the following engagements:

  • 10 PROS Advisory Board presentations/discussions spread across the four PROS Advisory Boards 
  • 7 staff-led pop-up community events, each at Division-specific locations 
  • 3 formal Council meeting presentations/updates for direction (not including RFP review or adoption or the budget allocation approvals)
  • 3 stakeholder group interviews with 18 individuals of varying interests 
  • 2 public open houses with over 250 total participants 
  • 1 half-day trails workshop with 25 diverse attendees 
  • 1 open-link public survey with 1,407 responses 
  • 1 resident-only, statistically valid survey with 766 responses
  • 1 additional 35-day publicly promoted feedback window to seek feedback on the final draft versions of the Guidebook via Engage Louisville 

Guidebook adoption is put forth via two separate resolutions – one for the LRP and one for the TSP. While both plans are part of the overall PROS Guidebook, the Long Range Plan sets a strategic direction for four PROS divisions (Parks, Recreation & Senior Services, Open Space, and Coal Creek Golf Course), whereas the Trail System Plan focuses on the future of the City’s shared pathway system and serves as a standalone planning document.


Since the presentation of both draft plans at the August 25th City Council meeting, staff and consultants have worked to incorporate Council feedback along with public input received during the final engagement window. At a high level, these refinements included: further copy-editing, streamlining plan terminology, better conveying the flow of the planning process, polishing plan maps and graphics, and refining the Action Plan Matrix to illustrate priorities and anticipated implementation timeline estimates. 


Staff recommend adopting the Guidebook resolutions to begin the new two-year budget cycle with renewed clarity on the PROS Department’s purpose and strategic direction for serving Louisville’s residents in the years to come.

This presentation will provide Council with updates on staff’s unified response to concerns related to electric motorized conveyances within the City of Louisville, and also present information related to current trends. The e-device concern on roadways has been noted in recent media reports and many jurisdictions across our State are taking action, including the City of Louisville. This update will present information about what staff has done over the last several years to address community and Council concerns related to e-bikes/e-motos and to discuss potential future strategies that may be developed to promote continued traffic safety in the community.  

This information will be presented by police command staff and the department’s crime prevention specialist.

children.name: September 2026 Meeting Minutes
Approving Consent and Acknowledgment for a Conditional Assignment of the LRC Grant Awards for the Grain Elevator
children.desc:
At the March 11, 2026 LRC meeting, the Louisville Revitalization Commission approved a grant award for the Grain Elevator property located at 540 County Road. This award included a 90% rebate of newly generated TIF, estimated at $216,000, a Façade Improvement Program grant of $72,500 and a Property Improvement Program award of $91,500. 

At the April 8, 2026 meeting, the LRC amended the Façade Improvement Program award by $36,000 to a total award of $108,500. Between all three grant awards, the total LRC commitment of $416,000.

The property owner, Louisville Mill Site LLC, requests approval of a Consent and Acknowledgment of a conditional assignment of the grants to DR Lending LLC, who is providing a construction loan for the project.

Public Hearing: Revitalization Commission Resolution 3, Series 2026 — A Resolution Approving Amendments to the Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2026 (advertised Boulder Daily Camera October ​18, 2026)
This will be the only reading of this item and final action may be taken. There will be one round of public comment.
children.desc:
The Louisville Revitalization Commission approved the 2026 budget in December 2025. Throughout the year, some budget changes have occurred that need to be formalized now in the 2026 budget. Those changes include 
  • $650,000 in Public Infrastructure Grants
  • $63,500 in Professional Services Fees
  • $225,480 in Façade Improvement Funds 
  • $161,530 in Property Tax Assessments
  • $1,982,600 Capital Improvement Funds for the Downtown Vision Plan 
  • $344,400 in Improvement Funds 

Staff is recommending approval of all changes and approval of the resolution to accept all amendments to the 2026 budget.

children.name: Discussion and Direction: 2027 Budget / Inital Approval
children.desc:
The Louisville Revitalization Commission (LRC) must approve a budget each year for the Urban Revitalization District (URD). The annual budget proposed by the LRC is then submitted to the Louisville City Council for review and approval prior to final LRC adoption before the end of the year. 

Staff is looking for feedback on the proposed 2027 budget with a recommendation for the LRC to send the budget to City Council for approval in November.

children.name: Resolution No. 95, Series 2026 — A Resolution Approving a Business Assistance Agreement with Arsenal Health LLC in the Amount of $208,400 for an Economic Development Project in the City of Louisville
children.desc:
Arsenal Health LLC is an integrated health optimization company looking to locate at 600 S. Pierce Avenue in Louisville. The business operates multiple locations in Colorado and Arizona and is looking to open a corporate headquarters and flagship health optimization center in Louisville in 2026.

The proposed location is estimated to generate between $4.3 million and $5.0 million in sales over the first seven years of operation at the Louisville location. The project represents an estimated $1.5 million in tenant improvements with additional investments in medical and laboratory equipment as the company continues to expand. 

The business anticipates having 15 employees at opening and 29 employees after three years. The average salary is anticipated to be around $80,000 with variable benefits. 

Staff is proposing an incentive of 50% of the eligible generated sales tax for five years, up to $200,000 (two hundred thousand dollars). In addition, staff is recommending a rebate of half of the building permit and sign permit fees with a not-to-exceed of $8,400 (eight-thousand and four hundred dollars).

docs.name: Arsenal Health Business Assistance Program Application

children.name: Resolution No. 96, Series 2026 — A Resolution Approving an Enhanced Business Assistance Agreement with Infleqtion Quantum, LLC in the Amount of $281,114 for an Economic Development Project in the City of Louisville
children.desc:
The City of Louisville provides new and expanding businesses incentive assistance through the Business Assistance Program (BAP). This program allows for rebates of building permit fees, consumer use tax and sales tax. Previous amendments to the program have also allowed for vacancy bonuses, enhanced assistance and small business support. The BAP program is regularly evaluated for effectiveness and needs to continue to support new and expanding businesses. 

The BAP application notes that Infleqtion Quantum is considering an expansion of office and lab space to accommodate growth related to recent contracts.  The expansion is anticipated to retrofit existing office space into a quantum lab space that includes quantum systems, precision optics and photonic systems, software and controls, research and development space, and engineering and testing space. 

Staff is proposing an incentive for Infleqtion Quantum with a not-to-exceed amount of $281,114.25.

docs.name: Project Lattice Business Assistance Program Application

children.name: Resolution No. 97, Series 2026 — A Resolution Approving an Agreement with the Boulder Watershed Collective in the Amount of $100,000 (for Wildfire Mitigation Program)
children.desc: Fire Smart Louisville, a voluntary, neighborhood-focused wildfire risk reduction initiative, began in early 2026 in response to the Wildfire & Conflagration Risk Assessment (WCRA). The program seeks to empower residents through education, expert guidance, and financial incentives, while coordinating resources across the City of Louisville, the Louisville Fire Protection District (LFPD), Boulder County, and partner organizations. Early accomplishments show strong community interest and demonstrated effectiveness. Fire Smart Louisville submitted a proposal for a scope of work for 2027 which recommended expanding and institutionalizing the program through funding a $100,000 contract with the Boulder Watershed Collective, enabling mitigation activities in high-risk neighborhoods and continued public outreach.

children.name: Resolution No. 98, Series 2026 — A Resolution Approving a Proposed 2026 Amended and 2027 Operating Plan and Budget of the Main Street Louisville Business Improvement District
children.desc:
The Main Street Louisville Business Improvement District (BID) is required to have its annual Operating Plan and Budget approved by the City Council as set forth in the C.R.S. 31-25-1211. The attached resolution amends the BID’s operating plan and budget for 2026 and approves an operation plan and budget for 2027 to align with the recently approved agreement with the City for the BID to operate the 2026/2027 Downtown ice-skating rink. 

Staff is recommending approval of the 2026 amended and proposed 2027 budget.

children.name: Proposition 123 Commitment
Resolution No. 99, Series 2026 — A Resolution Establishing Expedited Review Policies for Affordable Housing Projects
children.desc: Staff requests City Council approval of a resolution establishing an expedited review policy for qualifying affordable housing projects, as required under Proposition 123. Staff determined that the City's existing development review procedures can meet the state's requirements without code amendments. The resolution formalizes this policy to maintain eligibility for Proposition 123 funding.

children.name: Resolution No. 103, Series 2026 – A Resolution Approving Xcel Energy EV Infrastructure Rebates for the City's EV Charging Station Project
children.desc:
Staff requests City Council approval to accept seven Xcel Energy electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure and equipment (EVSI/EVSE) rebate reservations totaling $335,548.75.

The rebate reservations must be signed and returned to Xcel Energy by October 29, 2026, to preserve eligibility for this funding.

The reservations support potential electric vehicle (EV) charging installations at seven City-owned locations, including four facilities currently included in the City's Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and three additional locations being evaluated in partnership with Boulder County.

Approval of this resolution is limited to acceptance of the rebate reservations. It does not approve final charger locations, equipment purchases, construction, consultant contracts, or additional City expenditures. 

Staff will return to Council for subsequent approvals, including final project locations, implementation plans, funding agreements, and contracts, as applicable.

This will be the only reading of this item and final action may be taken. There will be one round of public comment.
children.desc:
613 Grant Avenue was landmarked in 2016 and received a landmark bonus of $1,000 but did not apply for any additional grant funding at that time.  The current funding resolution (Resolution No. 102, Series 2025) provides that owners are eligible to request grant funds subject to the funding resolution in place at the time of landmark designation, which in this case is Resolution No. 2, Series 2012. This resolution allows a Focused Preservation and Restoration Grant of up to $15,000 and does not include a time limit for application following landmark designation. 

The applicant is requesting a Focused Preservation and Restoration Grant of up to $15,000.00.

children.name: Monthly Revenue and Sales Tax Reports
children.desc:
Sales and Use Tax Collection Report – August 2026

Audit Revenue: Audit tax collections in August 2026 totaled $190,619. This revenue figure includes $40,678 in penalties and interest assessed on delinquent sales tax payments. YTD Audit revenue total for 2026 of $2,405,775.

Sales Tax: Increased MoM (August 2026 vs August 2025) by 20.9% for a total amount collected of $2,185,837. In-city businesses generated $1,056,243, an increase of $112,841 or 12%. Outside city businesses generated $1,129,594, an increase of $265,453 or 30.7%.

Cumulative Performance: YTD 2026 sales tax revenues exceed our budget by $1,700,105 or 11.1%. Compared to last year, sales tax revenue increased by $1,970,020 or 13.1%. All tax revenues combined YTD 2026, including sales tax, use, building, auto, lodging, bag taxes, and audit total $23,064,975. Removing audit, it is $20,659,200.

Consumer Use Tax: Consumer use tax collections for August 2026 amounted to $162,805, reflecting purchases brought into the city without the corresponding sales tax. Use tax remains an unstable revenue base due to its inherent unpredictability.

BAP Refund: Due to a significant BAP agreement, three new lines have been added to the Revenue History Report for tracking and reporting purposes.
